title: ToolSpec
description: A thin descriptor binding one MCP tool to one capability, carrying the metadata METIS needs and MCP does not itself provide (ADR-017). The registry resolves a CAP ID to one or more of these; policy chooses between them. Multiple ToolSpecs may satisfy the same capability — that is what makes hot-swap real.

version.description: SemVer of this implementation, independent of the capability's MAJOR.MINOR.

mcp.description: The MCP binding. Names the server logically and the tool within it; connection details (command line, URL, credentials) are deployment configuration, not contract, and deliberately do not appear here.

server.description: Logical server id, resolved to connection details by registry configuration.

tool.description: Tool name as advertised by that server over MCP.

idempotent.description: Whether calling this twice with the same input is indistinguishable from calling it once. Required, with no default, because durable execution replays (ADR-016) and a wrong guess here means a real-world side effect happening twice. A tool that sends, charges, or moves something declares false and must be dispatched through exactly-once handling rather than plain retry.

isolation.description: How strongly the tool is contained. `process` is the only honest value today: MCP servers are separate processes, so the boundary is the operating system's plus whatever METIS applies at dispatch (ADR-017). This is weaker than the container-or-WASM story in ADR-003. A single-valued enum rather than the old `sandboxed: boolean` — a boolean true would assert containment that does not exist, and adding `wasm` later is an additive change gated on a real WASM host and its own ADR.

authScopes.description: Scopes this tool requires. Policy denies at dispatch if a scope is not granted; a tool requesting an undeclared scope is a red-team case (REBUILD-PLAN Stage 5).

costs.description: Hints only. Planners must not treat these as authoritative (ADR-010).

tests.description: Conformance vectors. At least one is mandatory: ADR-006 requires a passing vector per capability version, and expressing it as minItems here makes the registry rule structural instead of a convention nobody checks.
